Supplementary manual verification, run by hand after scripts/publish-digest-stability.sh
aborted at its own self-check (see transcript.txt) on the same Docker daemon
(parallax-demo, Docker 29.1.3, storage driver overlayfs / io.containerd.snapshotter.v1),
in the same session, minutes later. These commands were run directly against the
real Docker engine and the real example-project/us-central1/parallax-demo Artifact
Registry repository -- nothing here is synthesised -- but they are NOT the script's
own output and are kept in a separate file from transcript.txt for that reason.

They exist because the script's extract_config helper cannot complete on this
Docker version (see transcript.txt and PROVENANCE.md for why), which stopped the
script before it reached Part 1's field-isolation step and all of Part 2. The
questions those steps would have answered are answered here by a different,
simpler method: diffing `docker image inspect`'s own JSON instead of the raw
config blob `docker save` exports.

===============================================================
== why extract_config's self-check failed: this daemon's storage driver
===============================================================

$ ssh 203.0.113.10 'docker info 2>&1 | grep -i -E "storage driver|snapshotter"'
 Storage Driver: overlayfs
  driver-type: io.containerd.snapshotter.v1

===============================================================
== isolating the differing field a different way: docker image inspect, not docker save
===============================================================
Same two images transcript.txt's Part 1 built and left addressable by their own
.Id (the tag was overwritten by build 2, but build 1 stays addressable):

  build 1: sha256:6a05b841795d32593433776443f8b7aa86d0f4fcf8a426425d79874baf25e1ef
  build 2: sha256:e2c9fbcae48dc0618e7ecb32bdfa2af1f604e0a1578a33cd028cd68b337e9a83

$ ssh 203.0.113.10 'docker image inspect sha256:6a05b841795d32593433776443f8b7aa86d0f4fcf8a426425d79874baf25e1ef > /tmp/build1.json'
$ ssh 203.0.113.10 'docker image inspect sha256:e2c9fbcae48dc0618e7ecb32bdfa2af1f604e0a1578a33cd028cd68b337e9a83 > /tmp/build2.json'
$ ssh 203.0.113.10 'diff /tmp/build1.json /tmp/build2.json'
18c18
<         "Created": "2026-08-11T06:09:31.105112677Z",
---
>         "Created": "2026-08-11T06:09:34.064436272Z",
20c20
<             "digest": "sha256:6a05b841795d32593433776443f8b7aa86d0f4fcf8a426425d79874baf25e1ef",
---
>             "digest": "sha256:e2c9fbcae48dc0618e7ecb32bdfa2af1f604e0a1578a33cd028cd68b337e9a83",
24c24
<         "Id": "sha256:6a05b841795d32593433776443f8b7aa86d0f4fcf8a426425d79874baf25e1ef",
---
>         "Id": "sha256:e2c9fbcae48dc0618e7ecb32bdfa2af1f604e0a1578a33cd028cd68b337e9a83",
26c26
<             "LastTagTime": "2026-08-11T06:09:34.121079474Z"
---
>             "LastTagTime": "2026-08-11T06:09:34.123604826Z"
29,31c29,35
<         "Parent": "sha256:5af960ebeec0fef64114ec24749b08122267643a4e4634572da76a230fcdf57d",
<         "RepoDigests": [],
<         "RepoTags": [],
---
>         "Parent": "sha256:63046cc8b331882a8ec6f19da36ab157dff1164b74cee97818616052975b63df",
>         "RepoDigests": [
>             "us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app@sha256:e2c9fbcae48dc0618e7ecb32bdfa2af1f604e0a1578a33cd028cd68b337e9a83"
>         ],
>         "RepoTags": [
>             "us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app:digest-stability-old-flow"
>         ]

Verdict: the top-level "Created" timestamp is the field that differs between
build 1 and build 2. Everything else that differs ("digest", "Id", "LastTagTime",
"Parent", "RepoDigests", "RepoTags") is a downstream consequence of that -- the
image ID is a function of the config content, which embeds "Created", so a
different "Created" produces a different ID and everything keyed off it. Both
builds resolved the same base layer (`---> 6d43704baacd` in both, transcript.txt
lines 75 and 99) and neither build passed --pull, so this is not base-image tag
drift in this run: the base layer was held byte-identical by construction and
the configs still differed until "Created" is accounted for.

This confirms the deploy/gcp/app/Dockerfile's "created" hypothesis, though by a
different diagnostic than the one the script itself was written to run, and
through the daemon's own inspect JSON's "Created" field rather than the raw OCI
config blob's "created" field the script's extract_config was written to read.
The two are very likely the same underlying value (docker image inspect's
top-level "Created" is documented as reflecting the image config's own
"created"), but that identity was not independently confirmed here because
extract_config could not run.

===============================================================
== the new flow: build once, push once, remove local copies, pull twice by
== manifest digest, and compare -- Part 2's core claim, checked without
== extract_config
===============================================================

$ docker build --no-cache -t us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app:digest-stability-manual ~/parallax/deploy/gcp/app   (via DOCKER_HOST=ssh://203.0.113.10, i.e. built on parallax-demo's own daemon)
...
Successfully built 70e54e9b2d3e
build .Id: sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54

$ docker push us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app:digest-stability-manual
...
digest-stability-manual: digest: sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54 size: 1401

Note: for this one build, the locally-computed .Id and the registry's manifest
digest are the same value. That is a real, observed property of this Docker
version's local image ID under the containerd snapshotter (see the storage
driver check above) -- .Id is evidently no longer simply the config-JSON
digest here, the way it was under the classic ("moby") image store the
predecessor plan's Dockerfile comment and this script's extract_config both
assumed. This is offered as an observation, not a claim about Docker's
internals verified any further than what is shown here.

$ docker rmi us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app:digest-stability-manual
$ docker rmi us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app@sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
$ docker image inspect us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app@sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
confirmed gone

$ docker pull us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app@sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
Digest: sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
Status: Downloaded newer image for us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app@sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
pull1 .Id: sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54

$ docker rmi us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app@sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
$ docker pull us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app@sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
Digest: sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
Status: Downloaded newer image for us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/example-project/parallax-demo/app@sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
pull2 .Id: sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54

VERDICT: IDENTICAL. Two independent pulls of the same manifest digest, with the
local copy fully removed and confirmed gone between them, produced the same
local image ID both times.

$ cargo run --quiet --bin parallax -- reference-value --image-digest sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
parallax: no --mrtd given, so the mrtd array is empty. MRTD measures the platform firmware, not the workload, so it cannot be derived from an image digest -- read it from a quote this platform produced.

$ cargo run --quiet --bin parallax -- reference-value --image-digest sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb8826ef9bfb415989b21a2c52e9c591aff12ccd32a34d0d54
parallax: no --mrtd given, so the mrtd array is empty. MRTD measures the platform firmware, not the workload, so it cannot be derived from an image digest -- read it from a quote this platform produced.
[reference_values]

VERDICT: IDENTICAL. `parallax reference-value` printed byte-identical output
both times, run from the same manifest digest.

===============================================================
== summary of what this file adds
===============================================================
Part 1's core claim (two --no-cache builds of unchanged source produce different
image identities) is established in transcript.txt itself (build 1 .Id !=
build 2 .Id) without needing extract_config at all. What this file adds to
Part 1 is the specific differing field, found by a different tool (`docker
image inspect` diff) after the script's own tool (`docker save` + diff)
proved incompatible with this Docker version.

Part 2's core claim -- that pulling by manifest digest twice, independently,
produces a stable local image identity, and that `parallax reference-value`
derived from that digest is a pure, repeatable function of it -- could not be
established by the script at all, because it aborted during Part 1. It is
established here instead, using the registry repository provision.sh created
for this task (deleted at teardown, per the task's resource-discipline
requirement) and the shared reference-value derivation the script itself would
have used. The digest exercised here (sha256:70e54e9b2d3e89bb...) is a scratch
tag pushed for this purpose only, distinct from both deploy/gcp/publish.sh's
real `:latest` publish and the digests recorded in examples/gcp-c3.toml.
